Write the resolved configuration of a run

Source: R/glow_config_write.R
write_resolved_config.Rd

Writes every setting of a resolved configuration, with the value in force, to config-resolved.yml in a folder. The file is the record of what a run used, and its settings read back, through read_glow_config, to the same values.

write_resolved_config(cfg, dir, provenance = list())

Arguments

cfg

A glow_config object from read_glow_config.

dir

The folder to write into. It is created when it does not exist.

provenance

A named list of what only the caller knows, for example list(glowanalyses = "0.4.0", command = "glow run snv_set --config my.yml"). Each element is a character, numeric or logical vector, and each name is used once. The names files, registry, root, packages and written_at are taken by the function.

Value

The path of the written file, invisibly.

Details

The settings are written section by section in the order of the registry. A logical is written as true or false, a number with the fewest significant digits (15 to 17) that read back to the same double, a named vector as a mapping, a function as its source text, and text that could be taken for a number, a boolean or a null in quotes. A character that YAML cannot hold as it is, such as a control character, is written as an escape.

Seventeen significant digits identify a double, so the text of a number is exact. Reading it back is R's conversion of text to a number. That conversion returns the same double for a number of up to 15 significant digits on every build of R, which covers a setting as a user writes it. For a number that needs 17 digits, or one near the largest or the smallest double, it is exact where R computes in long double (capabilities("long.double")) and can differ by one unit in the last place elsewhere, for example on Apple silicon.

Every value is checked against the registered type of its setting before anything is written: the R type, whole numbers and the range of an integer, infinity, the allowed words, and the fields of a map. A value that was changed to something its setting does not take stops the function with the setting named, so the function never writes a file that cannot be read back.

After the settings comes one reserved key, provenance, which read_glow_config() skips: the configuration files of the chain with their checksums, the registry with its checksum, the root for relative paths, the versions of GFisher, GLOWr and GLOWpipeline, the time of writing, and the caller's entries. The provenance describes the configuration that was written. A resolved file that is read and written again keeps its settings and gets a new provenance, in which the resolved file itself is the last file of the chain.

Computational complexity: linear in the size of the configuration.

See also

read_glow_config

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cfg <- read_glow_config("cohort0203.yml",
                        base = "base-config/base_config.yml",
                        registry = "base-config/settings-registry.yml")
write_resolved_config(cfg, "runs/cohort0203/baseline/training",
                      provenance = list(command = "glow run training"))
} # }
